chrome.name: Google Chrome

open_url_in_new_tab.name: open a web address in a new tab

steps.note: opens a new tab and jumps to it

open_url_in_current_tab.name: go to a web address in the current tab

find_on_page.name: find text on the current page

steps.note: mod+g moves to the next match

tips: These are the browser's own keys; web pages can define their own shortcuts on top of them.
An empty chord for one OS means Google's page lists no key that can be sent there; use the menu instead.
mod+1 to mod+8 jump to a tab by position; mod+9 always goes to the rightmost tab.
Tab switching differs by OS: ctrl+Tab on Windows and Linux, cmd+alt+Right on Mac.
mod+shift+t reopens closed tabs in the order they were closed.
Mac full screen is Fn+F, which uses the Fn key and is not listed as a chord here; hold Escape to leave full screen.
History and Downloads open as pages in a new tab.
On Windows and Linux alt+d and F6 also jump to the address bar.

discord.name: Discord

jump_to_dm_or_channel.name: open a direct message, channel or server by name

tips: ctrl+/ shows the full hotkey list inside Discord.
Escape marks the current channel as read; while a call is ringing it declines the call instead.
The vendor publishes these keys for Windows. Its macOS hotkey page is an image only, so the Mac keys are not listed here.
The vendor page lists two different keys for returning to the previous text channel, so that action is left out.

edge.name: Microsoft Edge

open_url_in_new_tab.name: open a web address in a new tab

steps.note: opens a new tab and switches to it

find_on_page.name: find text on the current page

steps.note: mod+g moves to the next result

tips: These are the browser's own keys; web pages can define their own shortcuts on top of them.
An empty chord for one OS means Microsoft's page lists no key for it there; use the menu instead.
mod+1 to mod+8 switch to a tab by position; mod+9 goes to the last tab.
Tab switching differs by OS: ctrl+Tab on Windows; on Mac the page gives cmd+Fn+Down, sent here as cmd+PageDown.
Mute tab is ctrl+m on both Windows and Mac; cmd+m minimizes the window on Mac.
History is ctrl+h on Windows and cmd+y on Mac; Downloads is ctrl+j on Windows and cmd+alt+l on Mac.
On Windows alt+d and F4 also select the address bar, and F5 reloads.

excel.name: Microsoft Excel

find_value.name: find a value on the sheet

steps.note: opens Find on Windows and Mac

go_to_cell.name: jump to a cell or named range

save_as.name: save the workbook under a new name

tips: An empty chord for one OS means the vendor page lists no key for it there; use the ribbon or menu instead.
Windows: tapping alt shows KeyTips letters on the ribbon; sequences such as alt+h a c are pressed one key after another, not held together.
Mac: function-key shortcuts (F2, F5, F8, F11, F12) may need Fn held unless macOS is set to use F-keys as standard function keys.
Mac: ctrl+Space, F11 and shift+F11 can collide with macOS system shortcuts and only work in Excel once the system shortcut is turned off.
Pressing select_all again widens the selection from the current data region to the whole sheet.
In the Windows Paste Special dialog each option has a letter: v values, f formulas, t formats, w column widths.
Delete (Backspace on a Mac keyboard) clears cell contents but keeps formatting and comments.
Return moves down after an entry by default; on Mac the direction can be changed in Excel preferences.

figma.name: Figma

run_action_by_name.name: run a command, tool or plugin by name

steps.field: action name, for example align or Keyboard shortcuts

place_object_with_keyboard.name: add a frame, shape or text layer without the mouse

steps.note: any tool key: f frame, r rectangle, o ellipse, t text

tips: The same shortcuts apply in the desktop app and in the browser editor.
Figma has no single web page of shortcuts; the full list is the in-app shortcuts panel (ctrl+shift+? on both Windows and Mac), with tabs by category.
With nothing selected, the arrow keys pan the canvas and shift+arrow pans further.
Lines, vector paths, connectors and tables need several clicks and cannot be placed with the keyboard alone.
Return enters a selected frame or group (select child); on a text layer it starts text editing, on a vector layer vector edit mode.
Holding Space gives the hand tool temporarily; holding alt while dragging duplicates the layer.
ungroup_selection also removes a frame around its children.
Shortcuts assume a US QWERTY layout; another layout can be chosen in the Layout tab of the shortcuts panel.

file-explorer.name: File Explorer

go_to_path.name: open a folder by its path

steps.note: search box; ctrl+f and F3 do the same

tips: Delete moves the selection to the Recycle Bin; shift+Delete removes it for good with no Recycle Bin copy.
ctrl+w closes the active tab, and the whole window when it is the last tab.
ctrl+1 to ctrl+9 switch to a tab by position; ctrl+shift+1 to ctrl+shift+9 change the view style instead (2 is Large icons, 6 is Details).
Backspace also goes to the previous folder, like alt+Left.
To pick several separate items, hold ctrl, move with the arrow keys and press Space on each one.
shift+F10 opens the context menu for the selected item.

finder.name: Finder

go_to_folder.name: open a folder by its path

steps.note: starts a search in the window

tips: The key Apple calls Delete is the one above Return (Backspace here): mod+Backspace moves the selection to the Trash.
mod+shift+Backspace empties the Trash after a confirmation dialog; adding alt skips that dialog, so leave alt out.
To move files: copy with mod+c, then mod+alt+v in the destination moves them instead of pasting a copy.
Open the selected item with mod+Down or mod+o.
Right and Left open and close a folder only in list view.
The Go menu in the menu bar shows the shortcuts for more common folders.

github.name: GitHub

find_file_in_repository.name: open a file in the current repository by name

steps.note: file finder; works on a repository code page

comment_on_issue_or_pull_request.name: post a comment from the focused comment box

tips: Press ? on any GitHub page to see the shortcuts that apply to that page.
Single-letter shortcuts depend on the page: c creates an issue on an issue list but opens the commits menu on a pull request Files changed tab.
Character-key shortcuts can be switched off in the account accessibility settings; shortcuts with a modifier key keep working.
The g-then-letter tab shortcuts work inside a repository.
The Markdown formatting shortcuts work in comment boxes and in the file editor.
Saved replies: ctrl+. opens the menu, then ctrl plus the reply number fills it in.
On an open issue or pull request, l, m and a apply a label, milestone or assignee; on an issue or pull request list they filter.

gmail.name: Gmail

steps.note: part of a name or the full address
moves on to the message body
reply to the sender; a replies to all

tips: The single-key and two-key shortcuts (c, /, r, e, #, x, g i, * a and the like) work only when Settings > See all settings > Keyboard shortcuts is on. The mod-key compose and formatting shortcuts are not tied to that setting.
Press ? to open the shortcut list. From there one Tab reaches a link named Enable or Disable; if it says Enable, Return turns the shortcuts on.
Single keys typed into the search box or a draft are text. shift+Escape moves focus back to the main window; Escape moves it to the latest chat or compose window.
Action keys apply to the open conversation, or in the list to the conversations selected with x. j and k move through the list (j older, k newer); o or Return opens the focused one.
In a new message Tab moves through To, Subject and the message body. In To, Cc or Bcc, type part of a name or address and press Return to choose the suggestion.
Drafts are saved on their own a few seconds after typing stops. Escape closes the compose window and keeps the draft; mod+shift+d discards it.
z undoes the most recent action, such as an archive or a move.
Users can remap keys under Settings > Keyboard Shortcuts (custom keyboard shortcuts), so a key may differ on some accounts. Shortcuts are also not supported on every language or keyboard.

google-calendar.name: Google Calendar

steps.note: saves from the event details page

tips: Shortcuts work only after they are turned on: Settings > tick "Enable keyboard shortcuts" > Save.
Press ? to see every shortcut. The help page lists j or n for the next date range but no key for the previous one; read it from the ? list.
Views have two keys each: 1 or d (day), 2 or w (week), 3 or m (month), 4 or x (custom), 5 or a (agenda).
delete_event acts on the selected event; Backspace does the same. z undoes the last change.
mod+s saves only from the event details page, and Escape returns from that page to the calendar grid.
The Keep and Tasks side panel is reached with Ctrl+Alt+. or , on Windows, Cmd+Option+. or , on Mac, and Alt+Shift+. or , on a Chromebook.

google-docs.name: Google Docs

run_menu_command.name: run any menu command with the tool finder

steps.note: opens the tool finder, which searches the menus
a command name or part of it, for example "spacing" or "rename"
moves into the list of matching results

tips: Navigation shortcuts are two keys pressed in turn while the modifiers stay held: Ctrl+Alt on Windows and Linux, Ctrl+Cmd on a Mac (next heading: n then h). Table shortcuts add Shift and start with t.
On Windows with a keyboard layout other than US English, many Ctrl+Alt shortcuts behave as AltGr and do not work as expected.
tool_finder (alt+/) searches every menu command by name; use it for anything without a shortcut, such as fonts or line spacing.

Menus on a Mac: Ctrl+Option+ f File, e Edit, v View, i Insert, o Format, t Tools, h Help. On Windows the same letters go with Alt in Chrome and Alt+Shift in other browsers. Then type the underlined letter of an item.
mod+/ opens a searchable list of every shortcut; Escape returns to the document.
show_outline opens the outline with keyboard focus: Down moves through the headings and Return jumps to one.
Every change is saved to Drive on its own, so there is no save step.
Holding shift with a movement key (word, line, paragraph, document start or end) selects the text passed over. In a table, Tab and shift+Tab move between cells.
open_link works when the cursor is on a link. PageUp and PageDown move by a displayed screen, not by a document page.
clear_formatting can also be ctrl+Space on Windows, and open_spelling_and_grammar can also be F7.
ChromeOS differs in places: the side panel is Alt+Shift+. and page up/down are Alt+Up and Alt+Down.
Some shortcuts might not work for all languages or keyboards.

google-drive.name: Google Drive
tips: mod+/ shows the shortcut list inside Drive.
Sequences such as alt+g i are the modifier chord first, then the letter on its own. alt is Option on a Mac.
On a Mac the create, upload and menu shortcuts use Control where Windows and ChromeOS use Alt (new folder: Control+c then f); the go-to and view sequences use Option.
Item shortcuts act on the selection in the items view. alt+g i moves focus to the items view; arrows move the selection and shift+Space toggles the focused item.
remove_selected also works as #. open_more_actions_menu can also be Alt+a on Windows and Control+a on a Mac.
Preview keys (Space, = and -, Escape) apply only while a file preview is open.
Some shortcuts might not work for all languages or keyboards.

google-maps.name: Google Maps
tips: Map keys work only when the map itself has focus: press Tab until the map is focused. A square then highlights part of the map and a numbered list of places in it appears below.
With the map focused, pressing the number shown next to a place opens details about it.
When the highlighted area holds more than 7 places, 9 shows more of them and 8 goes back.
Arrow keys move the map; with shift held they move it by one whole square.
ctrl+/ opens the list of shortcuts inside Maps. The help page gives this key as Ctrl only, with no separate Mac key.
mod+Plus, mod+- and mod+0 are the browser page zoom (bigger, smaller, reset), which enlarges what is on the page; the map zoom keys are Plus and - alone.

google-sheets.name: Google Sheets

insert_row_above.name: insert a row above the current row

steps.note: selects the whole row of the active cell
with a row selected this inserts a row above

insert_column_left.name: insert a column to the left of the current column

steps.note: selects the whole column of the active cell
with a column selected this inserts a column to the left
selects the whole row of the active cell
with a row selected this deletes it

tips: mod+alt+= and mod+alt+- depend on the selection: with cells selected they open the insert or delete menu; with whole rows or columns selected they insert above / to the left, or delete the selection, straight away.
insert_rows_below and insert_columns_right go through the Insert menu. On Windows the Alt+i form is for Chrome; other browsers use Alt+Shift+i followed by the same letters.
Menus on a Mac: Ctrl+Option+ f File, e Edit, v View, i Insert, o Format, d Data, t Tools, h Help. On Windows the same letters go with Alt in Chrome and Alt+Shift in other browsers.
tool_finder (alt+/) searches the menus by command name; mod+/ lists every shortcut.
The six number-format shortcuts use Ctrl on a Mac too, as do select_column (ctrl+Space) and toggle_compact_controls.
F1, F4, F9 and F2 in this guide apply while a formula is being entered. redo can also be mod+shift+z or F4.
rename_sheet (alt+1) is listed for Windows only. On a MacBook the sheet-switch keys are Option+Right and Option+Left instead of Option+Down and Option+Up.
On keyboards for Portugal, Italy, Germany and Spain the date and time keys differ: Ctrl+Shift+d for date, Ctrl+Shift+h for time, Ctrl+Alt+Shift+n for both.
Help > Keyboard shortcuts has a switch, "Enable compatible spreadsheet shortcuts", that turns on shortcuts used by other spreadsheet programs.
Every change is saved to Drive on its own, so there is no save step. Some shortcuts might not work for all languages or keyboards.

jira.name: Jira

comment_on_selected_work_item.name: start a comment on the selected or open work item

steps.note: the vendor pages give no key for saving the comment

tips: Press ? on any Jira page to open the shortcuts dialog; it shows the keys for the current operating system and browser, grouped as global, navigation, work item actions and app-specific.
Shortcuts can be switched off in that dialog; if single keys do nothing, check that the toggle there is on.
Some shortcuts need specific permissions or installed apps, so not every key works for every account.
In the text editor: / opens quick insert (tables, images and more), @ mentions a person, : inserts an emoji.
The editor accepts Markdown: **bold**, *italic*, `code`, "# " to "###### " headings, "* " or "- " bullets, "1. " numbered, "[]" action item, "> " quote, --- rule, ``` code block.

linear.name: Linear

open_issue_by_id.name: open an issue by its ID or title

steps.note: recent issues search; matches ID or title words

run_action_from_command_menu.name: run any action on the open or selected issues by name

steps.field: action name, for example Share issue or Remove parent

tips: The same shortcuts apply in the browser and the desktop app; the desktop app has fewer clashes with browser shortcuts.
A letter pair such as g i or o f is two presses in a row, not a chord.
Whether comments post with mod+Return or plain Return is an account preference; check before typing Return in a comment.
In the command menu, type i then a space to limit results to issues; p for projects, u users, t teams, l labels, f favorites, d documents.
With issues selected (x, or shift+Up/Down to extend), mod+k applies an action to all of them.
In an issue list or board, mod+b and mod+shift+s act on the view or selection; inside a text editor the same keys format text.
Deleted issues stay in the team archive (g x) for 30 days and can be restored there with #; mod+z right after a delete also restores.
Closing the new-issue dialog with Escape asks whether to keep it as a draft.
In the editor, / opens the formatting menu and Markdown is converted as typed.

linkedin.name: LinkedIn

steps.note: focuses the search box in the top navigation

tips: Hotkeys work on the desktop website only, and can be switched on or off in the menu that the Tab key brings up.
Press ? to open the site's own cheat sheet for the current page.
n (new post) works on the main feed; l, c, r and s act on a feed post only after moving to it with j or k.
j and k move through posts on the feed and through items on the Notifications page.
Go-to keys are two presses in a row: g, then the letter.
A highlight shows which element has keyboard focus.

mspaint.name: Paint

workflows.draw_freehand: Pick the Pencil in the Tools group, then drag on the canvas to draw.
workflows.draw_shape: Pick a shape in the Shapes group (line, rectangle, ellipse, triangle and so on), then drag on the canvas to place it; drag its handles to resize.
workflows.add_text: Pick the Text tool (the A icon) in the Tools group, click the canvas where the text goes, then type in the text box that appears.
workflows.fill_color: Pick the Fill tool (the bucket icon), pick a color in the Colors palette, then click inside an enclosed area.

layout.toolbar: top, under the title bar: tool groups such as Selection, Image, Tools, Brushes, Shapes, Size and Colors
layout.tools_group: Pencil, Fill, Text (A), Eraser, Color picker, Magnifier
layout.shapes_group: Line, Rectangle, Ellipse, Triangle, Arrow, Star and more
layout.colors_palette: color swatches at the right of the toolbar
layout.canvas: the large area under the toolbar where drawing happens
layout.status_bar: bottom: pointer position and canvas size

tips: Microsoft publishes no keyboard-shortcut page for the current Paint app, so only general Windows keys are listed; pick tools by their names in the toolbar.
The canvas is a drawing surface: read it with a screenshot and draw with drags planned from that image.
Choose the tool first (Pencil for freehand, a shape for geometry), then act on the canvas.
The Text tool needs two steps: pick the tool, then click the canvas to place the text box.
ctrl+z undoes the last stroke, so a wrong drag is cheap to take back.

notion.name: Notion

insert_block_with_slash_command.name: insert a block by type on an empty line

steps.field: / followed by the block name, for example /todo or /h2

tips: The same shortcuts apply in the desktop app and in the browser; new page, new window, new tab and reopen closed tab are listed for the desktop app only.
mod+k also opens search; with text selected it adds a link instead.
activate_current_block opens a page, checks or unchecks a to-do, opens or closes a toggle, or makes an image full screen.
Typing / opens the block menu: /text, /page, /bullet, /num, /todo, /toggle, /div, /quote, /h1, /h2, /h3, /code, /image, /toc. Escape closes it.
Markdown while typing: **bold**, *italic*, `code`, ~strike~; at line start "# ", "## ", "### " for headings, "- " bullet, "[]" to-do, "1. " numbered, "> " toggle, --- divider.
Typing @ mentions a person, page or date (a mentioned person is notified); [[ links a page; Escape dismisses the menu.
On Windows the ctrl+shift+digit block shortcuts can collide with other software that uses ctrl+shift.
The block actions menu (mod+/) has a text box: type an action, block type or color to change the selected blocks; it also edits several selected database rows at once.
Shortcuts are documented for English QWERTY keyboards.

olk.name: Outlook (new)

steps.note: new message, from the Mail view
moves to the next field; read which field has focus before typing

layout.sidebar: left: folder list (Inbox, Sent Items, Drafts and so on)
layout.message_list: center: messages in the selected folder
layout.compose: To, Cc and Bcc, Subject, then the body; Send button at the top-left of the compose area

tips: This guide is for the new Outlook for Windows (olk); classic Outlook uses different keys, for example ctrl+shift+m for a new message and alt+s to send.
Press ? outside a text field to open the app's own list of keyboard shortcuts.
Send is ctrl+Return; Return alone in the body only adds a line.
ctrl+n creates a message in Mail and an event in Calendar.
ctrl+f forwards the selected message; it does not open a find box.
ctrl+u marks a message unread in the message list, but underlines text while composing.
shift+Delete removes a message permanently instead of moving it to Deleted Items.
The app is web-based and can take a few seconds to render after launch; wait for the message list before sending keys.

outlook.name: Outlook (classic)

steps.note: new message window, from any view
moves to the next header field; Cc may sit between To and Subject, so read which field has focus

reply.name: reply to the selected or open email

tips: This guide is for classic Outlook on Windows (OUTLOOK.EXE); the new Outlook (olk) uses different keys, for example ctrl+n for a new message.
ctrl+n creates the item type of the current view (a message in Mail, an appointment in Calendar); ctrl+shift+m creates a message from anywhere.
Send is alt+s; ctrl+Return is also listed as send. Return alone in the body only adds a line.
The ctrl+number view keys can change with the app configuration; ctrl+1 Mail and ctrl+2 Calendar are the usual ones.
ctrl+f forwards the message here; it does not open a find box. Use ctrl+e to search and F4 to find text inside an open item.
ctrl+shift+i goes to the Inbox, but inside an open message it shows blocked external content instead.
Ribbon KeyTips such as alt+n a f (attach a file) are pressed in sequence inside a message window.
ctrl+shift+d deletes the conversation and ignores future replies to it.

powerpoint.name: Microsoft PowerPoint

steps.note: Find dialog on Windows, search field on Mac

save_as.name: save the presentation under a new name or format

tips: An empty chord for one OS means the vendor page lists no key for it there; use the ribbon or menu instead.
New slide is ctrl+m on Windows but cmd+shift+n on Mac; on Mac cmd+n makes a whole new presentation.
ctrl+d duplicates the selected object; the vendor page gives no separate Windows key for closing a presentation, so close it from the File menu.
Windows: ctrl+Return jumps to the next title or body placeholder and, from the last one, adds a new slide with the same layout.
With an object selected, Return enters its text; Escape steps back out to the object, and also ends a running slide show.
Slide-moving keys (mod+Up, mod+Down) act on the selected slide or section, not on text.
At the start of a line, typing * or - followed by Space starts a bulleted list.

reddit.name: Reddit

reply_to_selected_comment.name: reply to the comment selected with j or k

steps.note: opens the reply box for the selected comment

steps.name: reply_box_shows_intended_text
steps.note: the reply is public; confirm the text, then submit with alt+Return on Windows or cmd+Return on Mac

tips: Hotkeys work only on the current desktop reddit.com interface, not on old Reddit.
Submit is cmd+Return on Mac and alt+Return on Windows: wherever Reddit's list says CMD, Windows uses alt.
Press ? anywhere on Reddit to open the hotkeys panel, which lists every key and can turn hotkeys off or on.
Hotkeys are on by default; if a key does nothing, check the panel in case they were turned off.
Media keys reuse letters: j, k, l, f and c mean something else when they apply to the video player.
x expands or collapses content only in compact view.

slack.name: Slack

jump_to_conversation.name: jump to a channel or DM

tips: The same shortcuts apply in the desktop app and in the browser, except these desktop-only ones: preferences, upload file, jump to latest unread, Activity view, Threads view and browse channels.
The single-key message actions (e, t, f, p, a, u, m, r, Delete) work only while a message has keyboard focus, not while typing in the message field.
In a focused message, t opens its thread and r opens the reaction picker.
By default Up in an empty message field edits the last message sent; a preference can change it to move focus to the last message instead.
Escape marks the open conversation as read; shift+Escape marks every conversation as read.
mod+shift+h starts, joins or leaves a huddle in a conversation; inside a canvas the same keys open find and replace.
F6 moves focus between the sections of the window; use it to reach the sidebar or the message list.
Formatting shortcuts need the cursor in the message field; with a link on the clipboard, pasting over selected text makes it a link.
Some shortcuts differ on keyboards set to a language other than English. Shortcuts cannot be customized.

spotify.name: Spotify

search_spotify.name: search for a song, artist, album or playlist

tips: The same shortcuts apply in the desktop app and in the web player.
mod+/ shows the full shortcut list inside Spotify; the vendor page lists only part of it.
The vendor page does not list keys for next track, previous track or volume; use the on-screen player controls or check the in-app list.

teams.name: Microsoft Teams

go_to_chat_or_channel.name: open a chat or channel by name

send_long_message.name: write a formatted message in the expanded compose box and send it

tips: These are the desktop app keys. Teams in a browser uses different keys for many actions (for example search is ctrl+alt+e and the app bar is ctrl+shift+digit on Windows), so check mod+. there.
mod+. lists the current shortcuts. Shortcuts can be customized in the desktop app, so an account may differ from these defaults.
mod+digit follows the order of the app bar; the default order applies only if the user has not moved or added apps.
On Mac, cmd+shift+a answers an audio call and also toggles live captions in a meeting; cmd+shift+v accepts a video call or a screen share.
temporarily_unmute works only when Keyboard shortcut to unmute is on under Settings, Privacy.
mod+F6 and mod+shift+F6 move focus between the sections of the Teams window; use them to reach a pane before reading or typing.
The vendor lists shortcuts for the US keyboard layout.
In the Calendar, ? opens a dialog with more calendar shortcuts.

trello.name: Trello

steps.field: first letters of the board name

filter_cards_by_title.name: filter the cards on the board

steps.note: filter menu; the title search field is focused

add_card_below_selected.name: add a card below the selected card

steps.note: shift+Return instead opens the card right after creating it

tips: Card shortcuts (c, d, e, l, m, n, s, Space, label digits, move keys) act on the card under the mouse pointer or the open card, so select or hover the right card first.
c archives the hovered card at once. Undo (z) covers recent card actions, but deleting cards, lists or labels is permanent.
With a card open, Left or k opens the card above in the list and Right or j the card below.
paste_card_or_link: over a list it pastes a copied or cut card; on a board with text or a link copied it makes a new card; in an open card it attaches a copied link.
e opens quick edit for one card; with several cards selected (shift+click) it opens the bulk actions menu.
Shortcuts can be turned off under Account, Settings, Accessibility; if single keys do nothing, check that setting.
vote_on_card only works when the Voting Power-Up is enabled on the board.
In a comment, @ plus a name lists members; Return or Tab picks one and that member is notified when the comment is saved.

vscode.name: Visual Studio Code

open_file_by_name.name: open a file in the workspace by name

steps.note: Command Palette; F1 also opens it
ctrl on every OS, Mac included
F4 moves to the next result

tips: Any command can be run from the Command Palette (mod+shift+p), so it works as a fallback for an action whose key is unknown.
Two-step chords such as mod+k mod+s are pressed one after the other; in mod+k z the second key is pressed without the modifier.
These are the defaults for a US keyboard layout; users can rebind keys, and mod+k mod+s opens the editor that shows the current bindings.
Several keys use ctrl on Mac too: go_to_line, trigger_suggest, toggle_terminal, show_source_control and switch_recent_editor.
Close editor is ctrl+F4 on Windows, ctrl+w on Linux and cmd+w on Mac.
With nothing selected, cut and copy act on the whole current line.
find_next, find_previous and select_all_find_matches apply while the Find box has focus.
F11 is listed both for full screen (Windows and Linux) and for Step Into while debugging.
An empty chord for one OS means the vendor page lists no default key there.

whatsapp-web.name: WhatsApp Web
tips: All keys of a shortcut are pressed together.
The vendor lists keys for Windows and Mac only; the Windows keys are given here as the default for other systems.
The vendor page gives an incomplete Windows shortcut for Settings, so it is listed for Mac only.

word.name: Microsoft Word

steps.note: Navigation pane on Windows, search box on Mac

steps.name: replace_panel_open_with_find_text
steps.note: fill the replacement field, then review before replacing all

save_as_windows.name: save the document under a new name (Windows)

apply_heading.name: turn the current paragraph into a heading

steps.note: use 2 or 3 for lower heading levels

tips: An empty chord for one OS means the vendor page lists no key for it there; use the ribbon or menu instead.
Windows: ribbon KeyTips are tapped in sequence (alt, then h), not held together.
Replace is ctrl+h on both Windows and Mac; Go To is ctrl+g on Windows and cmd+alt+g on Mac (F5 on both).
Mac: F-key shortcuts may need Fn held; F8 and shift+F10 can collide with macOS system shortcuts.
Mac: F1 to F4 alone are undo, cut, copy and paste in Word, unlike on Windows.
mod+Return inserts a page break; shift+Return inserts a line break inside the same paragraph.
Pressing F8 repeatedly grows the selection from word to sentence, paragraph, section and whole document; Escape leaves the mode.
In a table, Tab in the last cell of the last row adds a new row.

x-com.name: X

steps.name: composer_shows_intended_text
steps.note: posting is public; confirm the text first

reply_to_selected_post.name: reply to the post selected with j or k

steps.note: opens the reply composer for the selected post

tips: These keys work on x.com in a desktop browser; press ? there for the site's own full list.
j and k move between posts; use them to put focus on a post before an action key such as l, r or t.
Go-to keys are two presses in a row: g, then the letter (g h for Home, g n for Notifications).
u mutes and b blocks an account, so treat both as consequential.
A standard post holds up to 280 characters.

youtube.name: YouTube

steps.note: focuses the search box at the top of the page
opens the results page; choosing a video title plays it

tips: Player shortcuts need focus on the player: in the current desktop layout, click the video player once before using them. Letters typed while the search box is focused are text.
Left/Right (5 s), Up/Down (volume 5%) and Home/End (start/end of the video) are documented for when the seek bar has focus. j, l, m, k and the digits are documented for the player as a whole.
Space plays or pauses only when the seek bar is selected; if a button has focus, Space activates that button. k toggles play/pause in the player.
The frame-step keys , and . work only while the video is paused.
shift+p works only inside a playlist. shift+n goes to the next playlist item or, outside a playlist, to the next suggested video.
f toggles full screen and Escape also leaves it. c toggles captions only when the video has them.
Chapter keys differ by OS: Ctrl with Left/Right on Windows, Option with Left/Right on Mac.
? (or the profile picture menu > Keyboard shortcuts) shows the full list. Hovering a player button also shows its key.
